meta.title: Commonwealth Electrical Technologies: the value-creation playbook (New England electrical/energy platform to Northeast infrastructure platform)
meta.method: Template events reuse Broad Sky, Smith + Howard and trade-press sources (Accounting Today, CPA Practice Advisor), checked 2026-10-06 against data/research/pp_nationwide.json and bsp_firm.json timeline. Vertical analogs (Pfingsten NEC Group, Ridgemont Crete United, Kohlberg Loenbro, IES Holdings) come from PE Hub, PrivSource and SEC 8-K pages. AI-agent, talent and growth-lever evidence comes from vendor case studies (Togal, Trimble Document Crunch, Bridgit, Procore, Newmetrix, Samotics, ServiceTitan), government sources (BLS OOH, DOL, mass.gov, CT DRS, EPA CWNS, NREL, ISO-NE, PJM) and banker/legal commentary (Taft, Capstone/IMAP, PKF, GF Data via Gulfstar). Expansion-phase data_points were computed with python3 from repo datasets: cet_opportunities (86 items), cet_wwtp_targets (183), ma_targets_cet (48 + pe_backed_competitors), cet_ne_counties (67), cet_filings (estimate_table), pe_landscape (overlap_with_bsp contains cet), serviceos_evidence (kpi_benchmark kb-cet-*, roadmap_assumption ra-cet) and bsp_firm. kpi_targets and kpi_roadmap are explicit analyst assumptions anchored to cet_filings pro forma estimates.
caveats: All CET revenue, EBITDA, headcount and margin baselines are low-confidence analyst estimates from cet_filings (PPP payroll, revenue per employee, comp margins). None is disclosed by CET or Broad Sky. kpi_roadmap and kpi_targets are labelled assumptions, not guidance.

Management guidance (bsp_firm thesis; Tyler's feedback) is no NYC expansion and a New England focus. The requested NY/NJ/PA leg is therefore Phase 4, a gated board option that explicitly excludes NYC. The repo has no NY/NJ/PA electrical target or opportunity dataset, so Phase 4 data_points are market-level only.

Smith + Howard add-on count: BSP's release says nine; named transactions reconcile to nine only if VIP Search and VIP Solutions count separately (see pp_nationwide caveats). Smith + Howard's "Horton, Lee & Burnett" add-on is unrelated to Horton Electrical Services.

Several sources returned HTTP 403 or timed out on direct fetch (PE Hub/Pfingsten, BusinessNC/Crete United, WaterMagazine/Samotics, ForConstructionPros/Newmetrix, Nasdaq/Procore, ecmag). Their claims were taken from search-engine extracts of those pages on 2026-10-06 and should be spot-checked before external use.

AI-agent metrics are vendor case studies or vendor claims for selected customers (Togal, Document Crunch, Bridgit, Newmetrix, Samotics, ServiceTitan), not controlled studies. Several come from general contractors or residential trades and are extrapolated to an electrical subcontractor. The Samotics figure is in GBP for a UK utility.
The FMI Capital Advisors 9-11x vs 6.5-8.5x recurring-service multiple claim is second-hand (quoted in a ServiceTitan blog, mechanical-contractor benchmarks) and was not read in the FMI original.

cet_opportunities est_value_usd is populated for only 43 of 86 items and reflects total project or program cost, not CET's electrical scope. WWTP project values are applicant estimates on draft/final SRF lists, not awards. Maine, NH and VT plants are not in cet_wwtp_targets.
ma_targets_cet revenue is ZoomInfo modeled; several figures conflict with headcount (e.g., JM Electrical $91M with 74 staff). Ownership is unknown for 26 of 48 targets.

CET appears as non-union on OSHA records (entity identity not independently confirmed). Union/merit-shop status of add-ons will constrain which apprenticeship lane and which public/utility work each crew can take.
Bonding/surety capacity, debt terms and DCAMM certification are not public (cet_filings data_gaps). The financing items infer structure; they do not report it.
meta.narrative: Tyler, CET can follow the Smith + Howard path: Broad Sky took a ~100-person, one-office Atlanta firm to ~800 people, 11 locations, nine add-ons and nearly 4x revenue in 3.5 years before selling to TPG. CET starts from a larger base, roughly 260-290 people, $65-100M of pro forma revenue and $6-11M of EBITDA after NuWave and Horton (low-confidence estimates from public filings), so the goal is ~3x in 36 months rather than 4x. Horton is the Market Street moment: the first adjacent-state add-on, which nearly doubles the workforce and brings Connecticut wastewater relationships. Phase 1 makes MA and CT one company and points Horton at 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects across CT, MA and RI, led by New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk. Phase 2 uses CET's existing six-state licensing to buy founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT from a 48-company screen with a ~$15.1M median, before Pfingsten's NEC Group, Ridgemont's Crete United or other sponsor platforms get there. Phase 3 is where the multiple moves: SCADA and pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency turn one-off bids into recurring contracts, the service mix that PKF and Capstone price 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors. Data-center electrical is a real upside in PJM (~30 GW of new load by 2030) but a thin one in New England, where ISO-NE says data-center growth has lagged other regions. Phase 4 into Upstate NY, New Jersey and eastern Pennsylvania stays a gated option outside New York City, consistent with management's New England focus, and opens only if month-24 targets are met. Nine AI agents do the delivery work: takeoff (~76% faster in a Togal test), bid-radar triage toward 30% win rates, contract review (~75% faster), crew scheduling, safety, solar and pump-station monitoring, field documentation and 24/7 dispatch. The constraint is licensed electricians, so the people plan pairs IEC merit-shop and IBEW-lane apprenticeships with MA and CT tax credits, a fast track to the journeyman license and broad-based equity for foremen. Financing follows the Horton precedent of delayed-draw debt plus seller rollover, with co-invest for the larger add-on wave; GF Data puts lower-middle-market total leverage around 4.0x. Every revenue, margin and headcount target here is a labelled assumption anchored to filings-based estimates, and should be replaced with CET's actuals in the first 30 days.

kpi_roadmap.note: ASSUMPTION. Oct 2026 pro forma run-rate inside cet_filings range ($65-100M revenue, $6-11M EBITDA, 260-290 staff); 10% margin = midpoint of 8-12%; locations = Worcester, Taunton, Norwell MA, Canton CT.
ASSUMPTION. Phase 1: ~8% organic (bid selectivity, Horton cross-sell) plus 2 tuck-ins (~$29M acquired revenue at the ~$15M target-screen median); margin ~10.5%.
ASSUMPTION. Phase 2 RI/NH/ME/VT add-ons (3-4 deals) plus Phase 3 recurring O&M lines; margin ~11.5%; also the Phase 4 gate test.
ASSUMPTION. ~3x month-0 revenue (Smith + Howard did ~4x in 3.5 years); margin 12.5%, just under IES ~12.8%; at most one Phase 4 anchor; ~25% recurring service mix.

items.phase: Phase 2 - Complete the six-state New England footprint (RI, NH, ME, VT)

items.phase: Phase 3 - Capability verticals that recur: water/wastewater O&M, solar + storage, EV fleet depots, data-center electrical, NuWave efficiency
geography: New England-wide; data-center work concentrated in Suffolk/Middlesex MA and Hartford/Fairfield CT
items.thesis: Shift the mix from one-off hard-bid construction to repeatable service and O&M contracts. That mix is what moves a contractor from the 5-6x project-heavy band toward the 10x+ service band. Offer four productized lines: (1) SCADA/pump-station monitoring for the WWTPs Horton wires; (2) solar + storage EPC and O&M with uptime guarantees, using the CT Energy Storage Solutions and MA SMART 3.0 programs; (3) EV fleet-depot make-ready and charger O&M, building on the MassCEC on-street charging prime role; (4) NuWave aeration, lighting and controls efficiency projects funded through Mass Save. Data-center electrical is an option, not the core: ISO-NE reports little data-center load in New England.

data_points.masscec_on_street_charging: 15 installation + 25 feasibility municipalities; up to ~450 Level-2 ports (cet_filings cet-018)
data_points.gridos_roadmap_assumption: GridOS investment $0.8-1.8M; 1.0-2.5 pts EBITDA margin; 0.5-1.5 turns multiple (serviceos_evidence ra-cet, est.)

market_evidence: ISO-NE CELT 2026: energy use +9% 2026-2035; New England "has not yet seen the same growth in data centers as other regions".
CT Energy Storage Solutions: 9-year program targeting 580 MW of distributed batteries; 140 MW moved from residential to C&I on demand.
MA SMART 3.0 effective Sep 12 2025: 900 MW for program year 2025, storage adders; state target 5 GW of storage by 2030.
Eversource MA Phase II EV program: ~$188M through 2026 for 150 DCFC and 8,200+ Level-2 ports.
NREL PV fleet: P90 availability 94.7% vs P50 99.1%, the uptime gap an O&M contract can close.

items.thesis: This phase is a board-level option, not a commitment. Management guidance is no NYC expansion and a New England focus, so Phase 4 opens only if Phases 1-3 hit the month-24 KPIs and a water/wastewater or mission-critical electrical target appears in NY/NJ/PA outside the five boroughs. The pull is demand: PJM forecasts ~30 GW of data-center load growth between 2025 and 2030, and NJ/PA wastewater needs are large. Entry would be one anchor add-on with its own licenses and union/merit-shop status, like Smith + Howard's Texas/Virginia moves. Broad Sky's NJ/PA presence (Thomas Scientific in Swedesboro NJ, Punctual Pros in Lancaster PA) gives local network but no electrical synergy.

items.lever: Bid selectivity (GridOS bid board + go/no-go scoring)
items.evidence: Public hard-bid work wins 10-20% (midpoint 15%); negotiated/selective work wins 30-50%. GridOS scores the 86 radar items (27 with fit >= 80) so estimators bid fewer, better-fit jobs.

items.lever: Recurring service / O&M share of revenue
items.evidence: Buyers start paying for recurring revenue at roughly 25% of the business (Taft). ServiceTitan cites FMI Capital Advisors (mechanical benchmarks): platforms with >40% recurring service command 9-11x adj. EBITDA vs ~6.5-8.5x below that. CET's current recurring share is not public (baseline null).

items.lever: Solar + storage fleet availability under O&M contract
items.evidence: NREL PV Fleet study (1,128 systems): 90% of systems were available >= 94.7% (P90); median 99.1% (P50). Monitoring plus truck-roll dispatch lets NuWave/Horton sell uptime guarantees.

items.lever: Non-productive project time (searching for data, rework, conflict)
items.evidence: FMI/PlanGrid (n=600) found 35% of construction professionals' time goes to non-optimal activities (~$177B/yr industry-wide). Target 28% is an ASSUMPTION (a ~20% relative cut from Procore + field agents), to be reset after a CET time study.

items.lever: Horton capture of funded/requested CT-MA-RI plant and pump-station projects
items.unit: % of eligible projects where CET/Horton bids electrical
items.evidence: cet_wwtp_targets lists 62 plant/pump-station projects (funded or requested) worth $2381.8M of total project cost across CT, MA and RI. Target is an ASSUMPTION; electrical is typically a minority share of total project cost.

items.lever: NuWave efficiency attach on Horton/CET wastewater accounts
items.unit: WWTP accounts with a NuWave efficiency project
items.evidence: 176 of 183 screened WWTPs carry an efficiency cross-sell flag (aeration/blower/UV/HVAC or >= 1 MGD). Aeration is usually a plant's largest electric load. Mass Save's 2025-2027 plan is funded at $4.5B. Target is an ASSUMPTION.

items.lever: Field labor utilization (crew scheduling across MA/CT)
items.evidence: Bridgit case study: for Skiles Group a 1-point utilization gain is worth ~$85K a year and 5 points ~$425K. Applied to ~275 CET staff, the dollar value would be larger (ASSUMPTION; CET baseline utilization not public).

cet_filings estimates CET at 8-12% EBITDA margin (midpoint 10%), benchmarked to Limbach ~10.4% and IES ~12.8% (FY2025 XBRL). Target = IES level, reached through bid selectivity, recurring O&M mix and shared back office.

items.lever: EV charging ports under management (CSMS + O&M)
items.evidence: MassCEC On-Street Charging: CET leads the vendor team for 15 installation municipalities, up to 3 sites each and 4-10 ports per site, so up to ~450 ports. Eversource MA Phase II (~$188M) funds 8,200+ L2 and 150 DCFC ports through 2026. A per-port subscription turns installs into recurring revenue.

Capstone/IMAP expect typical middle-market deals at 6.8x and premium deals at 9.8x in 2026 (a 3-turn spread). serviceos_evidence allows CET 0.5-1.5 turns from tech-enabled, recurring earnings; target = baseline + 1.5 turns (ASSUMPTION). PKF: project-heavy firms 5-6x vs 10x+ for repeatable service.

items.program: Merit-shop registered apprenticeship through IEC New England (CET + Horton as sponsors)
items.evidence: CET's OSHA records list it as non-union. IEC New England runs a nationally approved 4-year program in Rocky Hill CT (720 classroom hours; apprentices earn 8,000 OJT hours with their employer), 15 minutes from Horton's base.

items.program: IBEW/NECA JATC pipeline for union-required utility and public work (dual-track via union add-ons)
items.evidence: IBEW Local 103 and NECA Greater Boston reopened their Dorchester JATC after a $10M renovation; about 2,000 apprentices train there (10,000 OJT + 1,000 classroom hours). Targets such as McDonald Electrical (ANJ union division) give CET a union lane without converting the merit shop. Google is funding the Electrical Training Alliance ($15M) to train 100,000 workers and 30,000 new apprentices.

items.program: Apprenticeship tax-credit capture (MA RATC + CT construction-trades credit)
items.evidence: MA Registered Apprenticeship Tax Credit: 50% of apprentice wages up to $4,800 per apprentice per year, up to $100,000 per employer, refundable; $988,800 went to 50 employers for 206 apprentices in 2025. CT construction-trades credit: lesser of $2/hour, 50% of wages or $4,000 per apprentice.
items.metric: Up to $4,800 per MA apprentice per year

items.program: Licensed-journeyman fast track (8,000 hours + 600 classroom hours in MA)
items.who_it_helps: apprentices / project managers needing licensed supervision
items.evidence: Massachusetts requires 8,000 supervised hours over >= 4 years plus 600 classroom hours for the journeyman (Class B) exam. BLS projects 9% electrician growth (2024-34) and ~81,000 openings a year; DOL reports ~93% of apprenticeship completers stay employed. Paying for exam prep and tracking hours shortens time-to-license and retention risk.

items.program: Broad-based equity for licensed electricians and foremen (retention)
items.evidence: KKR's C.H.I. Overhead Doors gave all employees equity; at the 2022 sale to Nucor, hourly workers and drivers received ~$175K on average. Ownership Works reports most participating companies see lower turnover. With ~260-290 staff and a 3-4 year hold, a pool tied to the kpi_roadmap is a retention tool where licensed electricians are scarce (ABC: ~499K net new construction workers needed in 2026).

items.program: Horton 100-day integration and key-manager retention program
items.who_it_helps: Horton's 20 managers and 100+ field staff / municipal customers
items.evidence: McKinsey found ~70% of mergers miss their revenue-synergy targets, often from disruption and departures. Horton is third-generation (founded 1976, led by Warren Horton) and holds the CT wastewater relationships, so the plan keeps the brand and on-call 24/7 crews, sets retention agreements for named managers, and integrates estimating, safety and payroll first and the field last.

items.amount_or_range: $7.5M single-LP co-invest (Feb 2025); total Broad Sky equity in CET est. $25-45M
items.evidence: Form D for BSP-CET Co-Invest LLC: $7.5M sold to one investor, first sale 2025-02-05. Broad Sky's Mar 2026 Form ADV marks it at $8.504M (1.13x gross). The flagship fund reports $335M sold. A Phase 2 add-on wave can reuse the co-invest route instead of drawing only on the fund.

items.source_of_funds: Senior debt / delayed-draw term loan for add-ons
items.amount_or_range: Est. $25-55M pro forma after Horton (3.5-5.5x on $6-11M EBITDA); lender not disclosed
items.evidence: cet_filings found no BDC, lender press or UCC record naming CET, so the facility probably sits with a bank or a non-SEC-reporting lender. GF Data, lower middle market H1 2025: average total debt 4.0x TTM EBITDA, senior 3.1x, equity 57.3% of capital; business services priced at 7.5x. At month-24 EBITDA of ~$19.5M (ASSUMPTION), 4.0x supports ~$78M of debt capacity.

items.source_of_funds: Seller rollover and deferred consideration (Horton precedent)
items.amount_or_range: Not disclosed; Horton funded without a new Broad Sky Form D
items.evidence: The Horton acquisition vehicle was registered in CT with the CET LLC as principal, and no new Form D followed. cet_filings infers debt or delayed-draw plus seller rollover. Founder rollover also aligns sellers like Warren Horton through integration, as Pfingsten did with NEC's founder.

items.source_of_funds: Customer-side financing that funds NuWave / efficiency projects
items.amount_or_range: Project-level (NEIF commercial loans; Mass Save incentives)
items.evidence: CET is an approved contractor for National Energy Improvement Fund commercial energy finance across all six New England states. That lets customers finance efficiency and solar work off CET's balance sheet. Mass Save's $4.5B 2025-2027 plan and CT's storage incentives reduce the customer's net cost further.

items.source_of_funds: Operating cash flow and working capital discipline (pre-deal balance-sheet evidence)
items.amount_or_range: PPP-implied 2019 payroll $9.9M (CET) and $3.1M (Horton); both PPP loans fully forgiven
items.evidence: CET's $2.062M PPP loan (121 jobs) and Horton's $646K loan (42 jobs) were fully forgiven, and CET ranked #32 of 285 MA electrical contractors by PPP size. Local bank relationships (Webster Five, Collinsville/Northwest Community Bank) are candidates for equipment lines and surety introductions; bonding capacity (DCAMM certification) is an unverified data gap for public wastewater bids.
